messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for route `POST /v1/chat/completions` — p99=1580ms (threshold=1200ms). Impact: increased error budgets for a subset of customers. Paging @oncall-eng-sre :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): I see the page, jumping in. Can someone confirm if this is model-specific or route-wide? link: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/abc123/chat-latency

sam (sre): Looking. p95 also creeping up but less dramatic. This looks concentrated on requests routed to model-family `mistral-heavy` — volume for that model is up ~2.8x last 15m.

maya (oncall): ok — preliminary mitigation: can we flip fallback routing to `mistral-medium` for non-enterprise routes to shed load?

lee (platform): We have a fast fallback flag. Pushing to enable fallback for route-tag `chat:default` -> will route new requests to `mistral-medium` after the routing controller observes queue > 200ms. Doing a canary roll now. ops-bot: triggering rollout `route-fallback-2026-03-15`

ops-bot: deploy started: rollout/route-fallback-2026-03-15 -> 3/5 pods updated

maya (oncall): also enabling temporary per-route burst rate-limit to reduce head-of-line for customers sending long prompts (dev-team only). Sam please watch tails.

sam (sre): Watching. After fallback and burst-limits p99 dropped to ~980ms at 1765439120. p95 at 620ms. Looks like mitigation effective.

maya (oncall): Good. I want to capture adjustments we made so we can tune alerts. Current problem: default p99=1200ms triggered page for a high-volume model family during traffic spike. Need better per-model/per-route thresholds and a squelch story to avoid noisy pages.

tori (prod-metrics): Agreed. Proposal: introduce a "tiered squelch" rule and per-model baselines. Rough sketch:

```
# alert rule (pseudo)
ALERT ChatCompletionHighP99
IF p99(latency{route="/v1/chat/completions",model_family=~".*"}[5m]) > threshold_by_model[model_family]
FOR 3m
ANNOTATIONS {summary="p99 high for {{ $labels.model_family }}"}
```

Threshold matrix idea (examples):
- small/light models: p95=350ms, p99=850ms
- medium models: p95=600ms, p99=1200ms (current default)
- heavy models: p95=900ms, p99=1800ms (higher tolerance)

Also add noise gating: only page if deviation > X% from 1h baseline AND sustained for 3m. That removes transient blips.

lee (platform): We should also build a per-route "customer-class" dimension: enterprise vs self-serve. Enterprise routes keep tighter thresholds and immediate pages; self-serve gets higher squelch and optional automated fallback.

maya (oncall): For immediate follow-up: 1) capture the mitigation events, 2) add temporary annotation to the incident with decisions, 3) handoff to Lee to implement thresholds and dashboards. I'm going to create a ticket.

sam (sre): Quick note on false positives we saw historically: when KV cache warms or when GC on certain nodes happens, short p99 spikes happen across all models. Noise gating by baseline will help. Also suggest adding rate-of-change check: page only when p99 > threshold AND p99_current / p99_1h_median > 1.4.

maya (oncall): Agreed. For the follow-up change, please include an explicit canary window and per-route quiesce list (e.g., admin/test routes that we don't page on).

lee (platform): I'll own the implementation. Plan:
- Create new alert rule group `chat-latency-tiered` with model_family thresholds (yaml PR)
- Add a Grafana dashboard panel `Chat latency by model-family` with baseline banding and a quick toggle to view p95/p99
- Push alert rules behind a feature flag for 24h canary in staging then roll to prod next week

Here is an outline PR snippet I'll use:

```
# prometheus rules fragment
- name: chat-latency-tiered
  rules:
  - alert: ChatCompletionP99Tiered
    expr: |
      (quantile_over_time(0.99, latency_ms[5m])) by (route, model_family) > 
      bool label_replace(thresholds{job="chat-thresholds"}, "value", "$1", "model_family", "$1")
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: page
```

lee (platform): I'll add noise-gate annotation too. Will create dashboards with panels that surface per-route load and fallback events.

maya (oncall): Handoff to Lee for the change. I'll remain available for escalation. Summary for the ticket:
- Cause: traffic spike concentrated on `mistral-heavy`, thresholds too aggressive for heavy models
- Immediate mitigation: enabled fallback to `mistral-medium`, applied per-route burst rate limit for dev routes
- Outcome: p99 fell from 1580ms -> ~980ms within ~6 minutes of mitigation
- Next action: implement tiered thresholds + noise gating + per-customer-class routing policies + dashboard panels

ops-bot: incident annotated: mitigations and timeline saved to https://incidents.company/redwood/1765439000

maya (oncall): I'm handing this to @lee to implement the tiered rule and dashboards. Lee, please post the PR link and the production canary schedule.

lee (platform): Will do. Target PR today, staging canary 4h after merge, prod roll next Tue 09:00 PT. I'll also add runbook snippet: when p99 crosses model-specific threshold, check model QPS, fallback count, and KV cache hit-rate before paging.

sam (sre): Thanks team. After-action: let's schedule a 30-min sync with product to align enterprise vs self-serve thresholds and make sure customer-impact mapping is accurate.

maya (oncall): Incident resolved for now — latency stable and routing changes holding. Leaving thread open for follow-up items.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Alert ChatCompletionHighP99 for route `POST /v1/chat/completions` (1765439000) resolved at 1765439205.

lee (platform): PR opened: https://git.company/redwood/alerts/pull/782 - includes rule group & dashboard JSON. Starting staging canary at 1765439300 (scheduled).

maya (oncall): Thanks. I'll append a short blameless note and assign action items in the ticket.

tori (prod-metrics): I'll add the new dashboard panels and a short alert-sensitivity doc. Also adding a retention policy for the last 90d of per-model latency to help baselines.

maya (oncall): Closing the pager for now. Anyone else? :thumbsup:

sam (sre): :thumbsup: Good run.
